meta.reset: Reset DB, cache and search index to `fixtures` before every case. Fixture objects are flat (one object per advertisement). Ids are assigned sequentially in fixture order (1..8) and the id sequence continues from there, so the first advertisement created by a case gets id 9. Actor rows are seeded by the harness (email <name>@example.com, last_login null, permissions = session mask). Inject sessions directly. Fixture expiry timestamps are either far in the past (2001, 2004) or far in the future (2100+) so results do not depend on the wall clock.
meta.actor: Key into fixtures.actors, or: anonymous (no Authorization header), garbage_session, expired_session. Actor mask = actor.permissions when non-zero, else derived from caps (ads: create/edit/delete bits).
meta.request: path_params are unescaped and must be percent-encoded when substituted. headers: null removes a default header. body_raw (even empty string) overrides body. body_generator {json_padded_bytes: N, base} = valid JSON of exactly N bytes, padded with an unknown field.
meta.tokens: {$const: NAME} constants; {$repeat: {s, n}}; {$email_of_length: N}; {$raw_session: actor} session id without Bearer; {$actor_perms: actor} the actor's permission mask. Tokens appear only as direct field values (body, headers, path_params, assertion value).
meta.expect.body: empty | plain_text | json | any. Create (201) returns json {id, location}; update/delete (204) return empty.
meta.json_assertions: List of {path, op, value}. ops: eq, ne, type, len_eq, len_lte, gte, includes, excludes, is_null, not_null, unix_or_null (every element is an integer or null), sorted_asc, sorted_desc. Paths with [*] resolve to lists. is_null passes for both a missing field and an explicit null. includes/excludes on `groups` compare against the string values (the empty string is a valid value).
meta.eventually_ms: Retry the step until it passes or the timeout elapses (indexing is async).
meta.note: Free-text explanation of the assumption behind a case. Present on every case tagged `ambiguous` and on some inferred ones.
meta.semantics: PATCH always assigns expires_at: omitted or null resets it to null (never expires), so every PATCH that does not resend expires_at removes the expiry. GET /cms/ads/groups lists only groups that contain at least one non-expired ad; the search `groups` filter can return expired ads. expires_after/expires_before only match expirable ads (null expires_at never matches). Behaviour of the empty group is unknown, so every case that depends on it is tagged ambiguous.
meta.source: documented = rules inside the source_document; stated = rules given outside the docs (id/priority/group/expires_at rules, 406/413/415 conventions); inferred = derived from code (strings.go) or conventions.
meta.tags: boundary, cache, security, regression, verify_normalisation (needs case-folding), verify_char_counting (limits counted in characters), verify_clamp (ClampParams behaviour), assumes_distinct_bits (create/edit/delete are separate bits), undocumented_limit (limit comes from strings.go, not the docs), ambiguous (docs are silent/contradictory or the outcome depends on an assumption; expectation chosen by common sense, see note).
